verses.text: One day the wife of a man from the group of prophets cried out to Elisha, "My husband, your servant, is dead. You know he respected the LORD. But now the man he owed money to is coming to take my two sons as his slaves."
Elisha asked her, "How can I help you? Tell me, what do you have in your house?" She said, "Your servant has nothing in the house except a small jar of oil."
Elisha said, "Go around and borrow empty jars from all your neighbours. Get as many as you can.
Then go inside and shut the door behind you and your sons. Pour oil into all the jars, and as each one is filled, set it aside."
So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons. They kept bringing jars to her, and she kept pouring.
When all the jars were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another jar." He answered, "There are no more jars." Then the oil stopped flowing.
She went and told the man of God. He said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debts. You and your sons can live on what is left."
One day Elisha went to Shunem. An important woman lived there, and she begged him to stay and eat a meal. After that, whenever he passed by, he stopped there to eat.
She said to her husband, "I can tell that this man who often comes our way is a holy man of God.
Let's build a small room on the roof and put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp in it for him. Then he can stay there whenever he comes to us."
One day Elisha came, went up to the room, and lay down there.
He said to his servant Gehazi, "Call the Shunammite woman." So Gehazi called her, and she came and stood in front of him.

Elisha told Gehazi, "Tell her, 'You have gone to all this trouble for us. What can we do for you? Can we speak to the king or the army commander for you?'" She answered, "I live safely among my own people."
Elisha asked, "Then what can be done for her?" Gehazi answered, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
Elisha said, "Call her." So Gehazi called her, and she stood in the doorway.
Elisha said, "About this time next year, you will be holding a son in your arms." She said, "No, my master, man of God! Do not lie to your servant."
But the woman became pregnant, and about that same time the next year she gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had told her.
The child grew. One day he went out to his father, who was with the workers harvesting the grain.
He said to his father, "My head! My head hurts!" His father told a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
The servant picked him up and took him to his mother. The boy sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
She carried him up and laid him on the bed of the man of God. Then she shut the door and went out.
She called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and a donkey, so I can hurry to the man of God and come right back."
He asked, "Why go to him today? It is not a New Moon or a Sabbath." She said, "It will be all right."
She saddled the donkey and told her servant, "Lead on, and go fast. Do not slow down for me unless I tell you."
So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her in the distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, "Look, there is the Shunammite woman!
Run to meet her and ask her, 'Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is your child all right?'" She answered, "Everything is all right."

But when she reached the man of God on the hill, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came over to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone! She is in deep distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me. He has not told me why."
Then she said, "Did I ask you for a son, my master? Didn't I tell you, 'Do not raise my hopes'?"

Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tuck your cloak into your belt, take my walking stick, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet them. If anyone greets you, do not answer. Lay my walking stick on the boy's face."
But the boy's mother said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So Elisha got up and followed her.
Gehazi went on ahead and laid the walking stick on the boy's face, but there was no sound or sign of life. So he went back to meet Elisha and told him, "The boy has not woken up."
When Elisha reached the house, there was the boy, lying dead on his bed.
Elisha went in, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
Then he got on the bed and lay on the boy, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, and hands to hands. As he stretched out over him, the boy's body began to grow warm.
Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the house once. Then he went up and stretched out over the boy again. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
Elisha called Gehazi and said, "Call the Shunammite woman." So he called her. When she came in, Elisha said, "Pick up your son."
She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed down to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.

Elisha went back to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land. The group of prophets was sitting in front of him, and he told his servant, "Put the big pot on the fire and cook some stew for these prophets."

One of them went out into the fields to gather plants. He found a wild vine and picked as many wild gourds as his clothes could hold. He came back and cut them up into the pot of stew, not knowing what they were.
They served the stew to the men. But as they began eating, they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.
Elisha said, "Bring me some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Serve it to the people so they can eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot anymore.

A man came from Baal Shalishah, bringing the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread made from the first grain of the harvest, along with some fresh heads of grain in his sack. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat."
His servant asked, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" But Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat, because the LORD says, 'They will eat and have some left over.'"
So he set it before them. They ate and had some left over, just as the LORD had said.
